title: ECB forward rate guidance
instrument: Key ECB interest rates; basis-point changes refer to the deposit facility rate.

definitions.tightening: The Governing Council or its President speaking for it identifies a prospective increase or further rate normalization. The signal may be conditional.
definitions.easing: A possible reduction is explicitly included in the prospective rate path, as in an expectation for rates to remain unchanged or move lower. It does not imply a certain cut.
definitions.balanced: A clearly stated expectation that rates will stay at current levels, or explicit equal consideration of movements in both directions. The stance being maintained can be highly accommodative.
definitions.unclear: No sufficiently explicit rate direction or holding horizon is provided. Upside inflation risks or an actual hike alone do not establish guidance for an additional increase.

methodology: Selected public Governing Council announcements and official post-meeting press conferences. Press-conference observations include the President’s answers when they describe the Council’s position. Questions from journalists do not establish Council guidance.

Date is the release date. The deposit rate supplies the common basis for the action field; other key rates can move by a different amount. An individual speech, staff projection or asset purchase is not a future rate decision.
For an event study, time press-conference observations at the later conference, not the earlier release. A daily change may contain both. This panel does not report a measured market surprise.

A change is labelled only between verified consecutive monetary policy meetings with comparable source windows. Absence of a priorDate indicates that no comparison is made. A transition involving unclear records a change in explicitness.
Observations are selected across presidencies and policy regimes. Dates between observations are not assigned an imputed state.

observations.title: Introductory statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Duisenberg reported unchanged rates, warned that higher prices must not feed wage and price setting, and declined to indicate a future rate bias when questioned.
observations.analysis: Concern about second-round inflation and the removal of year-end liquidity did not specify a subsequent adjustment to official rates.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Willem F. Duisenberg reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council raised rates by a quarter point as monetary growth, credit and import prices increased inflation risks. Duisenberg asked listeners not to infer a directional bias from the size of the increase.
observations.analysis: The rise was an action taken. The Council’s spokesman did not announce an intention to repeat or reverse it.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Willem F. Duisenberg reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Trichet characterized the Council as particularly vigilant about upside inflation risks. In the questions that followed, he said a hike at the next meeting was possible but uncertain.
observations.analysis: The directional signal comes from his explicit contemporaneous description of the Council’s position. He expressly declined to pre-commit to a decision or a series.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Jean-Claude Trichet reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council increased all key rates by 25 basis points. Trichet said the Council had not decided this was the first of a series of increases and would watch inflation risks closely.
observations.analysis: March’s conditional next-meeting possibility had been realized. Vigilance alone did not identify the Council’s next rate action.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Jean-Claude Trichet reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Draghi announced that the Council expected rates to remain at their existing levels or below them for an extended period, based on subdued inflation prospects, weak activity and muted monetary dynamics.
observations.analysis: Holding and cutting were both consistent with the guidance. Only the downside was explicitly open as a direction of movement, without a commitment to cut.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council expected key rates to remain at existing levels at least through summer 2019, and longer if needed to keep inflation on its expected sustained adjustment path.
observations.analysis: This was calendar-based guidance to maintain rates, even as the Council outlined an eventual end to net asset purchases.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: Subject to confirmation of the inflation outlook, monthly net purchases would slow from €30 billion to €15 billion after September and end in December.

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: The Council kept rates unchanged. Draghi expected them to stay at those levels through at least the summer of 2019, with the duration tied to sustained inflation convergence.
observations.analysis: The opening distinguished an extended period of existing accommodation from a further cut. Reinvestment would continue beyond the start of a later rate increase.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: The Council held rates and extended its expected period of unchanged rates through at least the end of 2019. Draghi also announced another series of targeted longer-term refinancing operations.
observations.analysis: Moving the date of anticipated normalisation was a change in timing. The explicit near-term rate path remained flat, while targeted funding was a separate decision.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Draghi maintained the expectation of unchanged key rates at least through the end of 2019, with a state-contingent qualification tied to convergence of inflation.
observations.analysis: The Council retained its willingness to adjust its instruments if needed while specifying a flat rate path in its central scenario.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council expected existing rates to persist at least through the first half of 2020 and longer if needed for sustained inflation convergence toward its then-prevailing aim.
observations.analysis: The named horizon was for a stable rate level. It did not yet single out a reduction.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council planned to reinvest maturing asset-purchase holdings in full well beyond the point when it began raising rates.

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: In Vilnius, Draghi extended the period for which the Council expected rates to stay unchanged to at least the first half of 2020. Rates were kept at existing levels.
observations.analysis: Extending the date before which a hike was expected signalled accommodation through time. The Council still described its prospective rates as steady in this communication.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council retained its first-half-2020 horizon but now expected rates to be at current levels or lower. It also asked committees to examine possible further accommodation.
observations.analysis: Adding lower rates as an option altered the direction available under the guidance even though all three rates remained unchanged.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council asked for examination of the size and composition of potential new net purchases. The review was distinct from an actual restart.

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: The decision left rates unchanged. Draghi said that the Council expected them to stay at their existing levels or move lower at least through the first half of 2020.
observations.analysis: The explicit opening to lower rates changed the direction of the guidance relative to June. It was an option for a future decision, not a cut at the July meeting.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate fell to −0.50% while the other two rates stayed unchanged. The Council still expected rates to remain at current or lower levels until inflation convergence was convincing and visible in underlying inflation.
observations.analysis: The horizon became outcome-based. A delivered deposit-rate cut did not remove the stated option of further easing.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: Net asset purchases would restart at €20 billion per month in November, with the expected end shortly before the first rate increase.

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: The deposit rate fell 10 basis points to −0.50%. Draghi said key rates could remain unchanged or fall further until inflation convergence was established in projections and underlying inflation.
observations.analysis: The November restart of asset purchases reinforced the package. The rate clause separately retained the possibility of additional easing without naming a date for the next change.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Draghi kept the deposit rate unchanged and repeated that key rates could stay where they were or decline until sustained inflation convergence appeared in the outlook and underlying dynamics.
observations.analysis: The November purchase restart had been decided in September. The October conference continued the conditional easing bias with no further immediate change to the deposit rate.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Mario Draghi reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Introductory statement to the press conference (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: At her first monetary policy press conference as ECB President, Lagarde retained the expectation for present or lower key rates until projected and underlying inflation showed sustained convergence.
observations.analysis: Net asset purchases had resumed in November. The Council retained a possible rate cut in the stated future path even though its December rate decision was unchanged.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: After adopting the symmetric 2% target, the Council expected rates at current or lower levels until inflation reached 2% well before the forecast horizon ended, persisted there and underlying inflation had advanced sufficiently.
observations.analysis: The three conditions governed when prevailing accommodation could be withdrawn. A lower rate was permitted, not forecast as certain.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: Net purchases under the regular asset purchase programme continued at €20 billion per month. Pandemic purchases were managed separately.

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council left the deposit rate at −0.50% and expected rates to stay at existing or lower levels until its inflation tests were met. Those tests covered when inflation would reach 2%, its persistence and progress in underlying prices.
observations.analysis: Lower rates remained an express possibility, even as the Council confirmed a shrinking purchase schedule and described the sequence for an eventual first increase.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: Pandemic net purchases were due to end in March. The regular purchase programme was to buy €40 billion a month in the second quarter and €30 billion a month in the third.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde said a hike required the inflation tests to be satisfied and net purchases to have ended. She declined to renew an earlier assessment of the likelihood of a 2022 hike before the March projections.
observations.analysis: The president confirmed the existing framework but left the judgement on a hike open. A journalist cited the lower-rate option in the decision. The question supplies no new Council endorsement of a cut at the conference.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate stayed at −0.50%. The Council now expected existing rates to persist until its inflation tests were met. It placed any gradual adjustment after the end of net purchases, with an unspecified interval between them.
observations.analysis: Removing the earlier reference to lower rates changed the near-term guidance. A reference to eventual increases in the reinvestment arrangements supplied a sequence, while the rate paragraph still prescribed a conditional hold.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council accelerated the regular purchase schedule to €40 billion in April, €30 billion in May and €20 billion in June. Ending net purchases in the third quarter depended on the inflation outlook.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The opening statement expected rates to stay at prevailing levels until the inflation conditions were met. Lagarde confirmed that the Council had removed the earlier downward bias and left a gap between ending asset purchases and deciding rates.
observations.analysis: She said the interval could be as short as a week or as long as several months. Removing the lower-rate option changes the stated range of outcomes while leaving the timing and necessity of a hike conditional.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council retained the −0.50% deposit rate and its expectation that rates would remain where they were until its inflation conditions were satisfied. Any subsequent adjustment would follow the end of regular net purchases and proceed gradually.
observations.analysis: The incoming data made a third-quarter end to net purchases more likely. The Council continued to condition the first rate move on its inflation tests and left the interval open.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council said recent data reinforced its expectation that regular net purchases would end in the third quarter.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde described the Council’s agreed sequence as completing net asset purchases and subsequently deciding on a first rate increase and further increases. She gave a range of a week to several months for the possible interval.
observations.analysis: The answer clarified the contemplated direction after the purchases ended, without endorsing the number of increases priced by investors or specifying a first meeting.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council judged its inflation tests met, retained the −0.50% deposit rate and intended a 25 basis point July increase. It expected a further rise in September, potentially larger if the medium-term outlook persisted or worsened.
observations.analysis: The decision distinguished a sized July intention, a conditional September increment and, beyond September, a gradual succession of increases subject to the data.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council ended net regular asset purchases from 1 July while continuing to reinvest maturities.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council intended to lift its rates by 25 bp in July and expected another increase in September. Lagarde explained that the second step could be larger if the medium-term inflation outlook persisted or deteriorated.
observations.analysis: The July increment was an intention based on current information. September depended on a subsequent outlook and the accompanying end of net asset purchases was a separate decision.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: A half-point rise brought the deposit rate to zero, exceeding the step indicated in June. The Council considered more rate normalisation appropriate at upcoming meetings while returning to meeting-by-meeting decisions on size.
observations.analysis: An earlier exit from negative rates changed the pace. An explicit expectation of further normalisation preserved the upward direction.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council approved the Transmission Protection Instrument to address disorderly fragmentation. The decision established a facility without announcing purchases under it.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: After the 50 bp increase, Lagarde said the Council remained on a normalisation path. Frontloading meant that the earlier guidance tying the September increment to the July move no longer applied.
observations.analysis: The direction beyond the first increase survived the move to meeting-by-meeting decisions. Its size and the timing of the next step depended on incoming data. The new transmission instrument addressed fragmentation.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate rose to 0.75%. The Council expected additional increases over several meetings to curb demand and the risk that higher inflation expectations would become entrenched.
observations.analysis: The commitment to reassess at each meeting qualified the pace. The statement still specified a direction and a multi-meeting horizon.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: With the deposit rate positive, the Council suspended the two-tier remuneration of excess reserves. Flexible reinvestment under the pandemic programme continued.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Following the 75 bp step, Lagarde expected further increases over the next several meetings. Their size and speed depended on the data, particularly whether high inflation was becoming embedded in expectations.
observations.analysis: The purpose of frontloading was to withdraw accommodation faster. The president declined to turn one unusually large move into a fixed increment at subsequent meetings.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council raised the deposit rate to 1.50% and expected to increase rates again, with the path reassessed at each meeting. September inflation reached 9.9%, and price pressures had spread across the economy.
observations.analysis: The Council recognised substantial withdrawal of accommodation and retained the expectation of further increases. It no longer specified a number of upcoming meetings.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: From 23 November, outstanding targeted loans would be repriced against average applicable key rates over the remaining period, with additional early repayment dates. Minimum reserves would earn the deposit facility rate.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde reiterated that further rate increases were expected following the third hike in a row. Past tightening and its delayed effects would enter the assessment alongside the evolving outlook.
observations.analysis: Dropping the earlier reference to a number of meetings did not remove the upward direction. The conference gave no terminal rate or predetermined number of steps.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council increased the deposit rate to 2.00% and judged that rates still needed to rise substantially at a steady pace to reach sufficient restriction. Staff raised their projections despite the decline in the latest headline inflation reading.
observations.analysis: The smaller increase after two 75 basis point moves did not reverse the stated direction. The Council also emphasised the need to keep rates restrictive once the desired level had been reached.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The regular purchase portfolio was to decline by €15 billion per month on average from March through June 2023 through partial reinvestment.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde explained that additional increases would need to be substantial and proceed at a steady pace. On the information then available another half-point move was indicated for the next meeting, with later moves conditional.
observations.analysis: The reduction in today’s increment from 75 to 50 bp coexisted with a strong message about cumulative future tightening. The size of one decision and the prospective path conveyed different information.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council raised the deposit rate to 2.50%. It intended another 50 basis point rise at the March meeting because underlying price pressures remained strong, with the subsequent path to be reassessed afterwards.
observations.analysis: The next increase had both a size and a meeting attached. The Council gave less detail about what would follow it.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council set out how partial reinvestment would deliver the planned decline in the regular purchase portfolio, including a stronger tilt towards better climate performers among corporate issuers.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council intended a further 50 bp rise in March because of underlying inflation pressure. Lagarde described general agreement on that intention and said the path after March would be evaluated using the data.
observations.analysis: The March step was unusually specific. The Council retained discretion over the path beyond March, including how long a restrictive rate would need to remain in place.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council delivered the 50 basis point rise indicated in February, bringing the deposit rate to 3.00%. It said future choices would depend on the inflation outlook, underlying pressures and transmission amid financial-market tensions.
observations.analysis: The staff forecast predated the recent market stress. The Council provided decision criteria and offered liquidity support if needed, while leaving the subsequent rate direction and holding period unspecified.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The regular asset portfolio continued to run down by an average €15 billion a month through June. Liquidity support remained available if needed.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Asked about the future after the 50 bp decision, Lagarde said substantial further tightening was needed if the staff baseline held. The forecasts predated recent banking tensions and the Council could not yet determine a path.
observations.analysis: This is a conditional tightening scenario, with unusually high uncertainty about whether the condition held. The written decision supplied a reaction function without direction. Protection of financial stability and the rate outlook were discussed separately.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate rose to 3.25%. The Council said its future decisions would bring rates to sufficiently restrictive levels and then retain them there as long as needed. Underlying inflation remained strong while financing conditions were tightening.
observations.analysis: The future move toward sufficient restriction preceded a distinct holding phase. The Council supplied neither a size nor a date for the next step and acknowledged uncertainty about the impact on spending.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council expected to stop regular asset-purchase reinvestments in July.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported agreement that the Council was continuing to tighten rather than pausing. She described the 25 bp step as a return to a more usual increment after earlier large moves and said further ground remained under the baseline.
observations.analysis: The smaller increment allowed for evidence that policy was transmitting strongly. It did not imply that the Council considered the prevailing level sufficient.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council raised the deposit rate to 3.50% and continued to describe a restrictive level still to be reached and then sustained. Staff raised projected inflation excluding energy and food, particularly for 2023 and 2024.
observations.analysis: Slowing loan growth showed that earlier increases were passing through. Future movement towards sufficient restriction remained in the release, with its extent and timing dependent on the data.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council confirmed the end of regular asset-purchase reinvestments in July.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde judged a July increase very likely unless the baseline changed materially. She said the Council had not discussed taking a pause.
observations.analysis: The answer gave a clearer next-meeting direction than a general commitment to maintain restrictive conditions. No equally specific path was provided for meetings beyond July.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council raised the deposit rate to 3.75% and committed to setting rates at sufficiently restrictive levels for as long as necessary. It continued to assess the required level and duration from incoming data.
observations.analysis: July replaced the earlier formulation about bringing rates to a future level. It neither identified another increase nor judged the newly announced level adequate if maintained.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: Regular asset-purchase reinvestments had ended. The Council also set minimum-reserve remuneration at zero, a separate instrument from the deposit facility rate.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde narrowed the subsequent choice to another hike or a pause and explicitly excluded a cut. A pause could last only one meeting. New projections, inflation readings and transmission data would guide the decision.
observations.analysis: The label records the one-sided set of changes the Council contemplated. No probability was supplied for the hike relative to a hold. Coding this as an expected increase would overstate the statement.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate rose to 4.00%. Under its current assessment, the Council judged rates had reached a level which, maintained long enough, would materially assist the return of inflation to target.
observations.analysis: The new assessment directly identified the prevailing rate and its duration. The conditional holding signal left the Council free to respond to new information and set no calendar date.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council assessed that the rates already reached would contribute substantially to disinflation if sustained. Lagarde declined to declare a peak and said cuts had not featured in the discussion.
observations.analysis: The information concerned time at restrictive levels. The Council retained the option of a later increase if the incoming evidence required it.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate stayed at 4.00%. The Council repeated that holding rates at their current levels for long enough would materially help return inflation to target. Financing conditions were weighing increasingly on demand.
observations.analysis: The Council carried the September assessment into its first hold of the cycle. September's inflation decline included base effects, and the Council left the necessary duration dependent on the evidence.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: Lagarde said discussion of cuts would be premature and described a period of holding at rates assessed to be sufficiently restrictive. She left a subsequent increase possible.
observations.analysis: A hold conditional on transmission and inflation can be restrictive. Refusing to declare a peak leaves an upside risk without making another hike the stated path.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council kept the deposit rate at 4.00% and continued to judge that sustained restriction at prevailing levels would materially aid disinflation. The new staff projections put headline inflation at 2.7% in 2024 and 2.1% in 2025.
observations.analysis: The lower inflation forecast coexisted with elevated domestic labour-cost pressures and a conditional holding signal. The release gave no date for a cut.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council
observations.balanceSheet: The Council intended full pandemic-portfolio reinvestment in the first half of 2024, reductions averaging €7.5 billion per month in the second half and an end to reinvestment at year end.

observations.title: Monetary policy statement and press conference
observations.evidence: The Council again described sustaining current rates as a material contribution to reaching the target. Lagarde said it had not discussed cuts when asked about market pricing and emphasised domestic price pressures.
observations.analysis: The market’s prospective cuts and the Fed’s discussion were raised by questioners. The Council supplied a duration assessment without announcing a date for easing.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council held the deposit rate at 4.00%. It judged that keeping the rates already reached in place long enough would materially support the return of inflation to target. Decisions on the level and duration of restraint would still depend on incoming evidence.
observations.analysis: The reference to the prevailing rate levels supports a conditional hold. Neither a minimum number of meetings nor an unconditional promise to maintain 4.00% was given.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported a Council consensus that discussion of rate cuts was premature. It wanted more evidence on disinflation, including wages, while maintaining the rates it had judged sufficient if held long enough.
observations.analysis: She stood by her own earlier public remarks, but did not endorse the reporter’s description of a summer cut on the Council’s behalf. The holding signal was conditional on incoming evidence.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate remained at 4.00%. Despite lower inflation projections, the Council again identified the rates already reached as effective if sustained long enough. Domestic price pressures and wage growth remained elevated.
observations.analysis: The baseline language still pointed to maintaining current levels, with the duration contingent on economic evidence. The staff projection of inflation at 2.0% in 2025 was not a date for a cut.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde drew a distinction between a cut at this meeting, which the Council did not discuss, and loosening policy later, which it had begun discussing. Wage, profit and activity data would be more informative in June than in April.
observations.analysis: The Q&A opened a conditional path towards less restriction. June described when richer evidence would arrive. There was no agreed first-cut date, pace or size.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council kept the deposit rate at 4.00% and described when less restraint would be appropriate. It wanted greater confidence from the outlook, underlying inflation and transmission that inflation was converging sustainably towards target.
observations.analysis: This was an explicit conditional case for reducing policy restriction in the rate discussion. The Council did not name June, specify a size or commit to the outcome of its next assessment.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde described broad support for waiting for more evidence and said that a few members already had enough confidence. If the disinflation evidence held up, she saw a clear direction towards less restriction.
observations.analysis: The minority’s readiness to act in April concerned the timing of a cut. The Council’s conditional direction was stronger evidence than the named month or the minority view.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: After nine months of unchanged rates, the Council cut the deposit rate to 3.75%. It planned to maintain enough restraint to bring inflation to target, with future rate settings reassessed at each meeting.
observations.analysis: April’s condition justified the cut taken here. A promise to maintain adequate restraint can coexist with several future rate paths. The separately announced PEPP runoff also supplies no next-rate direction.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Asked whether a period of reducing rates had begun, Lagarde described further dialling back as likely if the data confirmed the disinflationary path. She distinguished the likely direction from the unknown speed and length of the adjustment.
observations.analysis: She declined to confirm a cutting cycle. One governor did not join the cut, but she reported agreement on deciding meeting by meeting. This is a conditional easing signal with a particularly uncertain pace.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council kept the deposit rate at 3.75%. Profits were absorbing some wage pressure, while services inflation remained elevated. It retained a conditional commitment to monetary restraint and would assess its degree and duration at each meeting.
observations.analysis: A hold at this meeting did not establish a holding period for 3.75%. The release defined the necessary stance against inflation without saying which way the next rate would move.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Asked directly about September, Lagarde said its outcome remained open. She attributed both the hold and the absence of a predetermined path to the full Council. Asked to repeat June’s signal, she pointed instead to the cut already delivered and uncertainty about wages, profits and productivity.
observations.analysis: The conference did not renew a prospective easing signal. Maintaining some degree of restriction was compatible with either another cut or an unchanged deposit rate.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate fell to 3.50%. The Council described this as a further reduction in restraint warranted now and kept future settings contingent on inflation and transmission. A previously announced corridor change also took effect.
observations.analysis: The deposit rate moved 25 basis points. The larger change in the refinancing rate reflected a narrower operational spread. Neither that adjustment nor the word “another” established that there would be a further cut.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde described the likely direction of the rate path as downward. She said the incoming evidence would determine how long cuts continued and when rates had been sufficiently restrictive, without specifying the sequence or the size of the moves.
observations.analysis: These answers added directional information beyond the decision release. Neither the 25-basis-point cut just delivered nor a question about a larger cut established the size of the next move.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council cut the deposit rate to 3.25% as inflation moved towards target and activity indicators surprised on the downside. It still expected a temporary rise in inflation and retained a meeting-by-meeting assessment of the required restraint.
observations.analysis: The statement explains why rates were reduced at this meeting. Slower activity and the expected path of inflation offer inputs to later decisions, without identifying the Council’s intended rate direction.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde explained that the common downward movement she had identified concerned inflation and economic indicators received before this cut. When asked about opening the door to a December move, she declined to do so and said the full set of evidence would determine the decision.
observations.analysis: More data at a projection meeting describes the information set. It is insufficient evidence of the direction or size of a further rate adjustment.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council cut the deposit rate to 3.00%. Past cuts were easing new loan costs, while earlier tightening still affected outstanding credit. It would reassess the appropriate stance as evidence arrived, without setting a path.
observations.analysis: The earlier formulation about keeping rates sufficiently restrictive was absent. This altered the description of the stance but did not identify a subsequent cut or a period of unchanged rates.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Discussing the removal of the earlier language on restriction, Lagarde described the direction of travel as clear while confirming that policy remained restrictive. In a separate answer she expressly described the downward path as contingent on inflation and transmission.
observations.analysis: Two-sided inflation risks did not cancel the conditional easing orientation. The Council had not decided the next move or debated a destination for a neutral rate.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate fell to 2.75%. New borrowing costs were easing, while some maturing loans still had to refinance at higher rates. The Council retained its case-by-case assessment of inflation and the transmission of policy.
observations.analysis: The bank distinguished a cut today from the lagged costs still reaching borrowers. Describing those costs does not give a direction for the next deposit rate setting.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde said that under the Council’s baseline and the evidence then available, rates were heading lower. She separated that direction from the sequence and speed, which the Council would determine using new information at each meeting.
observations.analysis: The answer supplied a baseline direction even though the release avoided a preset path. It gave no target for the cumulative cuts and no assurance that each meeting would deliver one.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council cut the deposit rate to 2.50%. It saw prior cuts reducing the restrictiveness of policy as new borrowing became cheaper, even as past increases still affected outstanding credit. Future settings would be determined meeting by meeting.
observations.analysis: A change in the degree of restraint describes transmission of the decisions already taken. The release gave no future rate level, intended direction or holding period.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde twice described the prospective choice as a cut if warranted by the data and a pause otherwise. Explaining the current decision, she reported one abstention and no opposition.
observations.analysis: A choice between a cut and a pause introduces easing as the one named direction. It does not mean a cut was more likely than a pause. Nor does the abstention identify a preferred future rate for the Council.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council reduced the deposit rate to 2.25%. Services inflation and wage growth had eased, while trade tensions were depressing the outlook and market volatility could tighten financing conditions. The next decisions remained contingent on new information.
observations.analysis: An expected tightening of market financing conditions is distinct from the Council raising its policy rate. The statement also did not make a commitment to another cut to offset those conditions.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Pressed on the disappearance of the description of the stance as restrictive, Lagarde explained why a neutral-rate comparison was difficult under trade shocks. She explicitly declined to give a direction for future rates and emphasised readiness to respond as the outlook changed.
observations.analysis: The unanimous 25-basis-point cut expressed a decision about current conditions. The question about the next direction and the discussion of neutral-rate uncertainty supplied no prospective Council choice.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate fell to 2.00%. Lower assumed energy prices and a stronger euro reduced projected headline inflation. Staff also described contrasting trade scenarios. The Council continued to reserve its rate decisions for each meeting.
observations.analysis: The baseline inflation undershoot in 2026 and alternative scenarios describe economic outcomes. They provide neither a policy-rate forecast from the Council nor an assurance that the cutting sequence is complete.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde described the Council as well positioned after the cut to 2%. When asked whether this meant a pause or a sideways path, she declined to characterise it that way. Subsequent steps would depend on the inflation outlook and the data.
observations.analysis: June’s answers described the starting position but deliberately stopped short of a prospective hold. The undershoot in the staff projection was not a signal for another cut either.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council held the deposit rate at 2.00% as inflation was at target and wage growth was slowing. It described exceptional trade uncertainty and would assess risks to inflation and transmission when setting rates at future meetings.
observations.analysis: Reaching the inflation target and pausing after several cuts do not by themselves express an expectation that 2.00% will hold for any particular period.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde described a wait-and-watch phase. Asked about market expectations of another cut, she said the Council was well placed to hold while it observed how risks developed over the coming months. She kept the response open if conditions changed.
observations.analysis: The time dimension and the explicit willingness to hold make this more informative than simply calling the present stance appropriate. It neither set a calendar commitment nor endorsed market pricing.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate stayed at 2.00%. Staff expected 2026 inflation of 1.7%, while the Council’s overall assessment of the inflation outlook was broadly unchanged. It reserved future rate settings for each meeting.
observations.analysis: A below-target staff forecast could matter for a future decision. It is not itself a declaration by the Council that another reduction will follow.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde distinguished the end of the preceding disinflation process from the end of rate cutting. She declined to characterise policy as a pause, a hold or a particular direction, and would not put a specific burden of proof on an increase, a cut or an unchanged rate.
observations.analysis: Listing the possible moves while declining to rank them gives no explicit view that increases and cuts were equally likely. The July willingness to wait was not extended for a further period.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council held the deposit rate at 2.00%, with inflation near target and activity supported in part by past rate cuts. Trade disputes and geopolitical tensions kept the outlook uncertain. The release preserved discretion over the future path.
observations.analysis: The Council identified sources of economic resilience and risks. It neither specified a future holding horizon nor discussed upward and downward rate moves as equal policy alternatives.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde explained that being satisfied with the current position did not mean fixing it in place. Asked about symmetry, she attributed symmetry to the inflation objective and retained a data-dependent approach to future settings.
observations.analysis: The symmetry of the inflation target does not assign equal weight to hikes and cuts in the current outlook. Nothing in the answer specified how long the present rate would remain appropriate.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The deposit rate remained at 2.00%. Staff lifted their 2026 inflation projection because services price growth was expected to slow more gradually, but the Council still expected medium-term inflation to stabilise at target. It declined to specify the rate path.
observations.analysis: An upward forecast revision and an unchanged current rate coexist here. Neither constitutes prospective guidance to tighten, nor does another hold convey a commitment to maintain the rate.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported unanimous agreement on holding rates at this meeting and preserving all options for subsequent meetings. Asked whether the Council had actually discussed a cut or a hike that day, she answered that it had not.
observations.analysis: The Council deliberately left the next rate and its timing unspecified. Open options do not establish that two opposite moves received equal consideration or that today’s hold would persist.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: With the deposit rate at 2.00% and medium-term inflation expected to stabilize at target, the Council committed to taking rate decisions meeting by meeting and disclaimed a pre-set path.
observations.analysis: An unchanged current rate and confidence in the inflation outlook did not establish a future holding period.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported a unanimous hold, described the economic risks as broadly balanced and explained that a stronger euro mattered through its effects on the outlook. She tied her favourable assessment of the current position to confidence about medium-term inflation.
observations.analysis: Her description of balanced risks referred to the outlook. She did not attribute an equal assessment of alternative rate moves to the Council or give a duration for the hold.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council left rates unchanged as the Middle East war raised near-term inflation and introduced downside growth risks. It would use the evolving outlook and transmission to judge the appropriate rate.
observations.analysis: The staff baseline put 2026 inflation at 2.6%. That conditional forecast was not Council guidance for a rate increase.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported a unanimous hold after discussion of the energy shock. She explained how the Council would monitor its duration, intensity and spread into prices and wages, and separated the adverse and severe staff scenarios from decisions on rates.
observations.analysis: Three figures around 2% for rates, inflation and expectations described the starting position. The indicators for responding to a shock did not specify a future rate direction.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council kept the deposit rate at 2.00%. Higher energy costs worsened inflation risks while weakening economic sentiment, and the Council retained its meeting-by-meeting approach.
observations.analysis: Describing risks in opposing directions did not amount to a symmetrical expectation about the next rate move.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde said all governors had debated whether to hike at this meeting before reaching a unanimous hold. A six-week wait for more evidence would clarify the energy shock’s duration and propagation. The two hikes in model assumptions came from the market path at the projections’ cut-off.
observations.analysis: A hike was a genuine alternative on the day. The Council did not say it expected to hike at a later meeting if the current assessment held up. A market assumption adds no independent Council signal.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council raised the three rates by a quarter point while reiterating that it would determine the stance from incoming information rather than commit to a path. Staff projected headline inflation of 3.0% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027.
observations.analysis: The increase was a response to the revised outlook. The decision did not specify another increase.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde described the 25-basis-point hike as unanimous and warranted across scenarios. In response to a question about a reversal, she said the new setting put the Council in a position to respond to developments and retained discretion at future meetings.
observations.analysis: She explained how the strength of a response could vary with the shock. That general rule and the decision already taken did not identify a further increase, a subsequent cut or an interval of unchanged rates.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council kept the deposit rate at 2.25%. Energy prices were volatile but near the June baseline, and the full inflationary effect of the shock had yet to emerge.
observations.analysis: After June’s increase it left both the next rate direction and the length of the pause open.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde reported that some governors had raised the possibility of a hike at this meeting, but she denied there was a push for one. The Council unanimously decided to hold and examine the incoming data before September. She identified the projected rate path as market-implied.
observations.analysis: Waiting for the next scheduled meeting set no expectation for what the Council would do there. The minority discussion and market path did not establish an agreed tightening preference.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: Another quarter-point increase took the deposit rate to 2.50%, with the staff baseline at 2.5% inflation in 2027. The Council again reserved decisions for each meeting as the outlook evolved.
observations.analysis: The higher 2027 inflation projection relative to June and the actual increase did not constitute a pledge of further increases.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: After raising rates, Lagarde explicitly said the Council had taken no view on the direction of its next move. Asked why forecasts above target did not themselves imply another hike, she pointed to the uncertainty and the need to reassess the evidence.
observations.analysis: Her answer distinguished the information used to decide from forward rate guidance. Neither the new rate level nor the baseline inflation projection supplied the missing direction.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position

observations.title: Monetary policy decisions
observations.evidence: The Council held the deposit rate at 2.50% as higher energy costs increased inflation risks and weighed on growth. It retained its data-dependent approach without pre-committing to a rate path.
observations.analysis: The release communicated a tension between inflation and activity. It did not describe either an expected hike or a period of stable rates.
observations.releaseWindow: Decision announcement, before the subsequent press conference.
observations.voice: Governing Council

observations.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A)
observations.evidence: Lagarde said the Council had weighed an immediate hike and unanimously waited for more evidence. If the incoming information confirmed the assessment that could already have justified an increase, she said the direction was clear to the Council. She repeated the condition when asked about December.
observations.analysis: This was a conditional upward signal after a hold. The release on its own left the rate direction open. Further wage and inflation data, energy developments and changes in financing conditions could alter the assessment.
observations.releaseWindow: Post-decision press conference, including official questions and answers.
observations.voice: Christine Lagarde reporting the Governing Council’s position
